title: Eviction-aware adaptive rate-bucket accounting for speculative KV prefetch
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Speculative prefix/KV prefetches can consume rate-limited tokens and quota without end-customer attribution when prefetches are later evicted or never used. This causes two practical issues: 1) tenant-visible throttling from speculative work that should be amortized or discounted, and 2) overcharging or opaque billing for background system optimizations.

Goal: Implement an eviction-aware adaptive rate-bucket accounting model that: (a) prevents speculative prefetches from causing immediate tenant throttles when safe to delay, (b) attributes costs correctly to request owners if prefetches are consumed, and (c) refunds or marks prefetch attempts as unbillable if evicted before use. The model must integrate with existing rate-limit bucketing and quota metering pipelines and support analytics for auditing.

Constraints: Must preserve user-facing SLOs, keep billing auditability, avoid large changes to the existing metering pipeline, and mitigate abuse vectors where tenants could game prefetch semantics to skirt quotas.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests that validate token attribution for prefetch hit vs prefetch-evicted cases
Metric and dashboard that shows prefetch-attributed vs speculative-unattributed token consumption
End-to-end canary rollout with no customer-facing increase in throttling for a pilot subset
Billing reports reconcile: <1% divergence from expected after rollout relative to the staging baseline
design_decision: Use per-prefetch metadata with a short-lived provisional bucket: prefetch requests draw from a provisional bucket that does not decrement tenant quota immediately. If the prefetched KV is later accessed by a real request within a configurable window (default 30s), we atomically transfer attribution to the request owner and deduct quota. If the prefetch is evicted before transfer or expires, mark the provisional usage as system-unattributed and emit refundable audit events (for accounting only). For extreme memory pressure or high speculative failure rates, throttle speculative prefetching via adaptive rate controls (exponential backoff per-tenant).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Simulation (2 weeks): Implement provisional-bucket semantics in staging metering; run synthetic workloads to validate accounting correctness and performance.
Phase 2 - Canary (1 week): Enable provisional buckets for 5% of production traffic; monitor throttles, billing deltas, and latency.
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp (2-4 weeks): Ramp to 50% then 100% with rollback gates if billing divergence >2% or throttles spike >1%.
Phase 4 - Audit and docs: Publish billing behaviour guide, update console billing FAQ, and run accounting reconciliation job for first 30 days post-rollout.
